proposed_fix.description: Confirm whether adservice is CPU-throttled and erroring, then, with human approval, modestly raise the CPU limit on the adservice container only if throttling is confirmed, while investigating the cause of the errors.
steps: Inspect adservice pods: kubectl top pod, container CPU usage vs requests/limits, and the container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods ratio.
Check adservice logs and recent deploys/config changes for the source of the 98% error rate (the errors are the primary symptom).
If throttling is confirmed alongside the errors, propose a bounded increase to the adservice container CPU limit (requests can stay the same), e.g. +50%, for human approval.
Apply the change via a normal rollout, then watch adservice_cpu, adservice_error and latency-90 for 10-15 minutes.
If CPU is not throttled, do not change limits; escalate to debugging the error source (dependencies, bad release, crash loops).
preconditions: Confirm adservice CPU is actually near its limit and throttled, not just elevated.
Confirm node has spare CPU capacity for the larger limit.
Confirm a human has approved the limit change and the current manifest is saved.
Check that no other rollout is in progress for adservice.
proposed_fix.rollback: Re-apply the saved previous adservice manifest (or kubectl rollout undo) to restore the original CPU limit.
